phase1.intro:
Time to make the blueprint idea actually branch.

What do you want to look at first?

topics.buttonText: How does one class build on another?
dialogue: [[term:Inheritance]] lets one class build on top of another instead of starting from scratch. `class Dog extends Animal` means [[key:Dog automatically gets everything Animal already has]] — its fields, its methods — without you retyping a single line of it.

stickyNote.flavor: 🌳 one class builds on another, no retyping
stickyNote.definition: class Dog extends Animal gives Dog all of Animal's fields and methods automatically.

topics.buttonText: What are superclass, subclass, and IS-A?
dialogue: `Animal` is the [[term:superclass]] (the parent, the more general blueprint), and `Dog`/`Cat` are [[term:subclass]]es (the children, more specific versions).
The relationship is called [[term:IS-A]]: a Dog IS-A Animal, a Cat IS-A Animal — which is exactly why `dog instanceof Animal` comes back true.

stickyNote.flavor: 👪 parent, child, and the relationship between them
stickyNote.definition: Superclass = parent/general blueprint. Subclass = child/specific version. IS-A describes the relationship (Dog IS-A Animal).

topics.buttonText: How does super(...) fit into a subclass constructor?
dialogue: Inside a subclass's constructor, `super(name, age)` calls the parent's constructor first, [[warn:and it has to be the very first line]] — you're letting Animal finish setting up its own fields before Dog adds anything of its own.

[[key:Why bother]] with all this? Code reuse (write eat()/sleep() once), extensibility (add bark() on Dog without touching Animal), and a clean hierarchy. One real limit: [[warn:Java only allows single inheritance]] — a class extends exactly one parent, never two.

stickyNote.flavor: ☝️ must be first, and only one parent allowed
stickyNote.definition: super(...) calls the parent constructor and must be the first line. Java allows a class to extend only one parent class.

phase2.errorMessage:
Test.java:8: error: cannot find symbol
        super(name, age);  // Error! Animal doesn't exist in this context
        ^
  symbol: variable super
  location: class Dog
Test.java:4: error: incompatible types: Dog cannot be converted to Animal
class Dog extends Animal {
                   ^
  class Animal not found
2 errors
phase2.explanation:
[[warn:Dog is trying to extend Animal, but Animal doesn't exist anywhere in this file]] — the compiler has genuinely nothing to inherit from. That's why it complains about `super` not being found — there's no parent constructor to call, because there's no parent class in the first place.

[[key:The fix is just writing the Animal class you meant to extend]] — the parent class needs to actually be defined and visible before Java can let Dog build on top of it. Multiple classes can absolutely live in one file, but every one you reference by name still has to exist somewhere.

phase3.openingDialogue: Let's build a family tree! Classes can inherit from each other~ 🌳

mcq.question:
What does 'Dog extends Animal' establish?

A) Dog and Animal are unrelated classes
B) Dog IS-A Animal — Dog inherits Animal's fields and methods
C) Animal now has access to Dog's methods
D) Dog can extend multiple other classes too

phase4.selfChallenge:
Create a Vehicle class with:
• Fields: brand (String), speed (int)
• Constructor
• Method: accelerate() — prints "[brand] is accelerating!"

Create a Car subclass that:
• Extends Vehicle
• Adds field: model (String)
• Constructor calls super
• Method: honk() — prints "[brand] [model] says: Beep beep!"

In main, create a Car and call accelerate() and honk().

phase5.trivia: [[fun:Fun fact]]: Java's designers deliberately left out multiple inheritance of classes — a feature C++ has — specifically to avoid something called the diamond problem, where two parent classes both define the same method and the compiler can't tell which one a shared subclass should use. Interfaces (which we'll get to soon) were Java's answer to getting some of the benefits of multiple inheritance without that mess.
phase5.openingDialogue: One more thing before you branch out further~
